3

The calendar (calendar.html) shows and edits calendars in the iCalendar format (.ics), the format of Outlook, Thunderbird, Google Calendar, Apple Calendar and most other calendar programs. Several calendars can be open at the same time.

Calendars

  • Open… (Ctrl+O) opens one or more .ics files; each becomes a calendar in the list on the left. You can also drop .ics files onto the window. In Chrome/Edge on the desktop, Recently used reopens calendars with one click.
  • New calendar creates an empty calendar.
  • The checkbox shows or hides a calendar, the colour field sets its colour, a double-click on the name renames it. A click on the name makes it the calendar for new and imported events.
  • Import events… adds the events of an .ics file (e.g. an invitation received by e-mail) to the selected calendar. An event with the same UID replaces the existing one, so an updated invitation updates the event.
  • 💾 saves a calendar: directly into its file in Chrome/Edge on the desktop, as a download in Firefox and on Android (replace the original file with it). Save all (Ctrl+S) saves every changed calendar; changed calendars are marked with •.

Everything in the file that the calendar does not edit (further reminders, participants, tasks, other properties) is kept when saving.

Views

View Key Content
Month M six weeks; a click on a day number opens the day
Week W time grid of the week with a line for all-day events; the red line is the current time
Day D time grid of one day
Agenda A list of the events of the next 60 days
Availability F free and busy times of the week, one row per calendar (see below)

Today (T), ‹ and › (←/→) navigate; the small month on the left jumps to a date. The week starts on Monday or Sunday (setting at the bottom left). Search (/) shows only events whose title, location, description or categories contain the text.

🖨 prints the current view with the names of the shown calendars and the period as heading (month and week on landscape sheets, the whole day on one sheet); with "Save as PDF" as the printer you get a PDF. The search applies to the print as well.

Availability (free/busy)

The Availability view helps to find a time that suits several calendars, e.g. your own calendar and the calendars or free/busy files of colleagues. For every day of the week it shows the working hours with one bar per shown calendar: busy times in the calendar's colour, tentative events (status "tentative") hatched. Events marked as "free" (transparent) and cancelled events do not count; all-day events (birthdays, holidays, trips) only count when the file marks them as busy. The green row Free shows the times in which all shown calendars are free for at least the chosen duration; the list below repeats them. A click on a free time opens a new event at that time.

Working hours (e.g. 8 to 18), Duration (min) and Weekends set what is searched; the settings are remembered. Export free/busy (.ifb) saves the busy times of the shown calendars for the next eight weeks as an iCalendar free/busy file (VFREEBUSY) – without titles or other details, so it can be shared to tell others when you are available. Free/busy files from others (.ifb, e.g. published by Outlook or a calendar server) can be opened like calendars; their busy times appear in the availability view (they have no events for the other views) and are kept unchanged when the calendar is saved.

Creating and changing events

  • New event (N), a double-click on a day in the month view, or dragging over a time range in the week or day view opens the event dialog.
  • In the week and day views, drag an event to move it (also to another day) and drag its lower edge to change the end. In the month view, drag an event to another day.
  • A click on an event opens it for editing.

The event dialog contains title, calendar, all day, start and end, time zone, repetition, location, description and categories. Export (.ics) downloads the event as a file, e.g. to send it by e-mail.

Time zones

New events use the time zone of the computer. An event keeps its time zone; for example, a meeting at 9:00 in New York is shown at the corresponding local time. Times of events from Outlook with Windows time zone names are converted correctly. "Floating" times have no time zone and are always shown at the same clock time.

Repeating events

Repeat: daily, weekly (on selected weekdays), monthly (on the same day of the month or, e.g., on the third Monday) or yearly, every n days/weeks/months/years, ending never, after a number of times or on a date. More complex rules from other programs are shown as "Custom rule" and kept unchanged.

When you change, move or delete an occurrence of a repeating event, the calendar asks whether to change only this occurrence or all occurrences.

🔔 Reminder sets a reminder at the start or a time before it (5 minutes to one week); it is stored in the file as an alarm (VALARM), so other calendar programs show it as well. Reminders appear while the calendar is open in the browser: as a message at the top of the window or, after switching on 🔔 in the toolbar (the browser asks for permission), as a system notification. A closed page cannot remind you. Reminders that were due more than five minutes before the page was opened are not shown again.

Undo (↶, Ctrl+Z) and redo (↷, Ctrl+Y) cover new, changed, moved and deleted events, imports and the name and color of calendars. Opening and closing calendar files are not undone.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.

On phones and tablets

The agenda view is the default; ☰ opens the calendar list and the small month. The other views work as well; in the week view the days are narrow, so the day view is often more practical.
